title: link_load_balance.c has the same negative-left-shift UB fixed in rf_health.c
description: Out-of-scope note from the 205c security codereview: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/link_load_balance.c:32 uses '(int32_t)snr << 16' — identical C11 UB to what worker6-205c fixed in rf_health.c:45 (left shift of negative signed; LoRa SNR is routinely negative). Line 88 also has the unclamped '(avg_fp + (1<<15)) >> 16' rounding that 205c clamped in rf_health.c snr_avg (reviewer notes its EMA is bounded so overflow is not reachable, but the shift UB is live). Apply the same two fixes: multiply by FP_SCALE instead of shifting, and consider the same clamp shape if the accumulation can saturate. Verify with the R-APPC-011 gate command (must stay exit 0) and a standalone behavior check like the one used in 205c.
close_reason: Fixed the negative-left-shift UB in lichen_lb_update_snr (lichen/subsys/lichen/link/link_load_balance.c:32): '(int32_t)snr << 16' replaced by '(int32_t)snr * (int32_t)LICHEN_LB_FP_SCALE' — the explicit signed cast is required because the macro is 65536u (unsigned multiply would wrap rather than stay in signed domain). Semantic equivalence holds for all int8 inputs (max |snr_fp| = 8,388,608 << INT32_MAX; diff overflow-safe by EMA convex-hull induction, reviewer-verified). The rounding clamp from rf_health was deliberately NOT added: this EMA has no saturation path, avg_fp + 32768 is provably in-range ([−8,355,840, 8,355,840]) and the (int8_t) cast is exact — rationale documented in a comment. Verification: standalone behavioral check (10-sample sequence incl. INT8_MIN/INT8_MAX extremes: EMA converges sanely, SF thresholds react, min/max tracked, clean compile under -Wall -Wextra -Werror — module has no committed host test yet, noted in close); R-APPC-011 gate still exits 0. Codereview 3x (Kimi K3) all PASS, no findings: correctness (semantic equivalence + unsigned-cast necessity), security (UB previously could yield garbage SF selection on attacker-influenced negative SNR — now defined; overflow analysis confirmed), edge-cases (INT8 extremes, no other signed shifts missed, no-clamp reasoning verified). Non-defect observations noted, pre-existing: (int32_t) cast on the shift amount is a no-op; lichen_lb_update_snr lacks a header declaration (linkage hygiene).
